name: Sentry

pages.text:
The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically. You can use the APIs to manage account-level resources, like organizations and teams, as well as manage and export data.

If you're looking for information about the API surface for Sentry's SDKs, see the SDK Development docs.

The current version of the Sentry's web API is considered **v0**. Our public endpoints are generally stable, but beta endpoints are subject to change.

While many of Sentry's APIs use `sentry.io` as the host for API endpoints, if you want to indicate a specific data storage location, you can use your region-specific domain. Using your organization's region-specific domain will generally result in lower latency for most API calls. For example, if you are hosted in the US region, you would use `us.sentry.io`. You can check which region your organization is in by viewing your organization’s settings page.

To find out which API resources are available on region-based domains, see what types of data are stored where for more information.

If you're building on top of Sentry's API (i.e using Auth Tokens), you'll need certain scopes to access different API endpoints.

To set the scopes for an integration token, select the scopes from the dropdown. These can be edited later.

To set the scopes for an personal token, select the scopes from the dropdown when creating a personal token. These cannot be edited later.

The `project:releases` scope will give you access to both **project** and **organization** release endpoints. The available endpoints are listed in the Releases section of the API Documentation.

Be aware that if you're using `sentry-cli` to manage your releases, you'll need a token which also has `org:read` scope.

Authentication tokens are passed using an auth header, and are used to authenticate as a user or organization account with the API. In our documentation, we have several placeholders that appear between curly braces or chevrons, such as `{API_KEY}` or `<auth_token>`, which you will need to replace with one of your authentication tokens in order to use the API call effectively.

For the string format of auth tokens, organization tokens, DSNs, and legacy API keys, see Token and Credential Formats.

Some API endpoints require an authentication token that's associated with your user account, rather than an authentication token from an internal integration. These auth tokens can be created within Sentry on the "User settings" page (**User settings > Personal Tokens**) and assigned specific scopes.

For third-party applications that need to access Sentry on behalf of users, Sentry supports OAuth2 with the authorization code grant type. This allows users to authorize your application without sharing their credentials.

A Sentry user can belong to multiple organizations. The access token only provides access to the specific organization the user selected during the OAuth flow. The `/api/0/organizations/` endpoint will only return the connected organization.

# List an Issue's Events | Sentry Docs
GET /api/0/organizations/{organization\\_id\\_or\\_slug}/issues/{issue\\_id}/events/
Return a list of events bound to an issue.

### Scopes
You need to [authenticate via bearer auth token.](https://docs.sentry.io/api/auth.md)
`` requires one of the following scopes:
\* `event:admin`
\* `event:read`
\* `event:write`
```
curl https://sentry.io/api/0/organizations/{organization\_id\_or\_slug}/issues/{issue\_id}/events/ \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer '
```

This pricing applies to organizations on Sentry’s **latest** pricing plan. For information on older plans that include transactions or performance units based billing, go to your **Settings > Subscription** page.

Sentry offers a 14 day free trial with unlimited event data on the Business plan. You can upgrade or return to the features and quotas included with your existing plan. Without a paid plan, you will be automatically assigned a free Developer plan at the end of your trial.

Every paid plan includes a preset volume of event data, with a PAYG bugdet that you control. The free Developer plan has similar presets. See Sentry's plan page for more details.

Sentry offers several products, each of which have their own pricing structure as listed in the tables below. Paid pricing plans include a standard volume of events for each product or data category and you can buy more either by prepaying for reserved volume and/or setting up a PAYG budget.

Size Analysis helps mobile development teams monitor and reduce mobile app size, which can help improve install and uninstall rates. It breaks down your mobile apps so you can see exactly where size is coming from, and surfaces insights that recommend specific fixes. Every organization has 100 size analysis builds that can be uploaded per billing period. Additional builds are only available through an Enterprise Plan. If you’d like to explore Enterprise plan options, email sales@sentry.io to discuss pricing for additional builds.

**Plans and Pricing** → Sentry offers a free Developer plan and three paid plans (Team, Business, and Enterprise). Each paid plan includes a base volume per data type, and you can add more with discounted reserved volume or a pay-as-you-go budget, all billed by the amount of data you send. Sentry has a 14-day free trial with unlimited event data and access to Business plan features. At the end of the trial, you can upgrade or return to the features and quotas included with your existing plan. If no plan is selected at the end of your trial, your organization will default to the free Developer plan. Learn more about pricing and billing.

* **Alerts** — notify on new errors, regressions, error spikes, or when thresholds like error rate, latency and crash-free session rate are crossed
* **Uptime monitors** — watch your endpoints for downtime
* **Cron monitors** — track scheduled jobs for failures or missed runs

| Feature | What it adds | Set up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tracing** | Follow requests across services, find slow queries and N+1s | Enable `tracesSampleRate` in SDK config |
| **Agent Tracing** | Trace and debug agent workflows and conversations | Read the instructions for your SDK |
| **Logs** | Structured logs alongside errors and traces | Add log calls or a logging integration — set up guide |
| **Session Replay** | Video-like recordings of user sessions (web and mobile) | Enable replay in SDK config |
| **Profiling** | CPU profiles showing which functions are slow | Enable profiling in SDK config |
| **Application Metrics** | Custom counters, gauges, distributions | Add metric calls to your code |
| **User Feedback** | Collect bug reports from users, linked to errors | Add the feedback widget |

* **Dashboards** — pre-built views for frontend, backend, mobile, and AI performance, plus custom dashboards
* **Trace Explorer** — search, filter, and aggregate span data to find performance bottlenecks
* **Releases** — track crash-free sessions, version adoption, and regressions by deploy

The **Sentry Cookbook** has step-by-step recipes for common workflows, including debugging with MCP + Cursor, setting up AI observability, creating dashboards with agents, and more. Full recipes live on sentry.io/cookbook.
